issues.description: Method identifier mismatch: the problem statement (UML and textual requirements) requires a static method named acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) on class SealSaloon, but the solution implements a static method named receiveDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) in SealSaloon. This naming inconsistency means students implementing the method as acceptSupplyDelivery (as described) will not match the solution's API, and automated tests or references that expect acceptSupplyDelivery will fail to find the method.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the API name consistent. Rename the solution method receiveDelivery to acceptSupplyDelivery with the signature: public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity). Alternatively, add a public static wrapper method acceptSupplyDelivery that delegates to receiveDelivery, and update any tests or documentation to use the single name acceptSupplyDelivery so students and automated checks reference the same method.

issues.description: Identifier naming mismatch for the same concept: the problem statement (UML and text) specifies a static method named 'acceptSupplyDelivery(String, int, int)' on SealSaloon to receive ingredient deliveries. The provided template Main.java also calls SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery(...) in its example usage. However, the solution implementation declares a static method named 'receiveDelivery(String, int, int)' in SealSaloon. Because these three artifacts refer to the same operation with different names, students following the problem statement or the template Main will look to implement or call 'acceptSupplyDelivery', while the solution (and any tests derived from it) uses 'receiveDelivery', causing confusion or compilation/runtime mismatches.
issues.suggestedFix: Unify the method name across artifacts. Rename the solution's static method 'receiveDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)' to 'acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity)' and update any internal references. Alternatively, update the problem statement and template Main usage to call 'receiveDelivery'—but prefer renaming the solution method to 'acceptSupplyDelivery' to match the problem statement and example code.
